readback_body:
## Requirements: Execute Sandbox Filesystem RootFS, mounts and managed Workspace declarations

### Problem and verified baseline

[#3405](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/3405) records the client-safe Filesystem declaration (`filesystem.rootfs`, `filesystem.mounts[]`, `filesystem.workspace`, with `filesystem.access.read/write` unchanged) and defers executable behavior to a follow-up Requirement. The current V1 runtime still accepts only `filesystem.access` or an Agent-prepared `filesystem.composition`; a client declaration had no execution path.

This Requirement implements the first executable slice:

- the canonical protocol declares RootFS, additional read-only image mounts and a Workspace selection;
- `nession-sandbox::compile` validates the declaration against the Agent-prepared composition and refuses an unmaterialized or inconsistent declaration;
- the Server derives the existing `SandboxImageSelection` transport from the declaration and still mints scoped grants only after Ready/digest checks;
- Enter resolves a managed Workspace (explicit stable id, explicit name, or Session-name `auto`), acquires its RW lease, and binds its durable directory at the implicit `/workspace` target; execution cleanup releases the lease without deleting bytes.

### Explicit current limits

- Project Existing Location selection is not resolved yet; a `project_location` selection is refused.
- A managed Workspace combined with a Project EROFS lower (Overlay upper/work inside the managed directory) is refused; that separate contract remains deferred.
- Leases are in-memory; durable reconstruction from execution records after an Agent restart is follow-up work.
- The current mount target restriction remains `/opt/<lowercase-name>` and mounts remain read-only.
- The Web five-section Filesystem editor and Distribution UI are separate UI integration work.

### Success Criteria

- [x] SC-01 The canonical `filesystem` declaration accepts RootFS (`local` or one `base_runtime` image digest), zero or more read-only image mounts with validated `/opt/<name>` targets, and a Workspace selection with at most one stable id/name; `compile` refuses an unresolved declaration, a RootFS/mount digest that disagrees with the prepared composition, duplicate/overlapping or writable mounts, and an invalid or contradictory Workspace reference, without silently dropping a field.
- [x] SC-02 On an authenticated preflight or Enter, when the client sends the Filesystem declaration without an explicit image list, the Server derives the Base/toolchain selection, requires every derived digest to be Server Ready, and mints exactly the same scoped grants; an explicit image list that disagrees with the declaration, or a local root carrying mounts/Workspace, is refused before Agent routing.
- [ ] SC-03 On a supported Linux Agent, Enter with a managed Workspace selection resolves/creates exactly one stable Workspace, acquires its RW lease, binds that durable directory at `/workspace`, and reports the effective policy; execution cleanup releases the lease, leaves the bytes intact, and a second attachment observes the same content. A missing directory, a lease conflict, an unsupported Project Location/lower combination, or an unavailable registry refuses preparation with no Native fallback.

**SC → scenario:** SC-01/SC-02 → SCN-01 (source-aligned protocol/compiler and handler deterministic fixtures at the exact PR SHA). SC-03 → SCN-03 (existing approved Linux EROFS/Sandbox Case lane; source-aligned isolated Agent preparation and cleanup).

## Acceptance Plan

```yaml
acceptance:
  SC-01:
    when: pr
    method: agent
  SC-02:
    when: pr
    method: agent
  SC-03:
    when: merged
    branch: staging
    method: case
```

| SC-03 | Pending | awaiting merged staging SHA native Linux Case |

## Prototype

- **Decision:** Not needed as a separate prototype. The interaction was already defined by the #3405 five-section Filesystem design and its pinned prototype; this Requirement is runtime/protocol execution. Web presentation is separate UI work.

## E2E Verification

### New
- none: runtime/protocol behavior; source-aligned Cases cover the declarations and managed Workspace attachment

### Regression
- sandbox-workspace-capability

## E2E Report

| ID | Type | Result | Evidence |

| sandbox-workspace-capability | Regression | Pass | run 43473173148/2, SHA ad38ccb317743e2fad31c0c58d5a56f9822519e1, contract 8c22f02cce472ccbea35b36b4b2471d5c6f388cb19c3de09c782f8152aa37de7, plan f1e3c4711c53a1e6e97be360bdb5f8324b4ebb54be15742b2e373b23818a25c1, tests 20/20 (https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/actions/runs/43473173148) |

## Product alignment

- [ ] Session-scoped Sandbox and the Server-owned image registry stay authoritative.
- [ ] Client declarations never carry raw Agent image paths or bearer grants.
- [ ] Managed Workspace bytes outlive the execution; cleanup releases only the mount/lease.
- [ ] Unsupported combinations fail closed rather than silently applying a subset.

Related: #3405, #3407, #3024, #3408.

---
**Status:** Approved
